patch_description: Key insight: the previous programs spent most of their time recomputing ALL 165 triangle areas for every candidate move. Since only one point moves per step, only the 45 triangles containing that point change — so we maintain a full area vector and update just the affected entries, making each local-search evaluation ~4x cheaper. This lets us afford many more restarts AND a new post-restart crossover/merge phase: we take the top-3 configurations found by independent restarts, build merged candidates (5 points from one config, 6 from another, projected into the triangle), and re-run the shrinking directed-perturbation loop on each — exploiting the evidence that independent restarts saturate around 0.77 while complementary sub-arrangements may combine better. Moves are *directed*: we always perturb a vertex of the current worst triangle (best-of-K batched Gaussian candidates), which focuses search effort exactly where the objective is bottlenecked. Warm starts are boundary/lattice-heavy (vertices + edge points + jittered lattices) since Heilbronn optima are known to place most points on the boundary.
